newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe sends vote observers to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe sends vote observers to Albania.

text.p: The Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly said on Tuesday it would send observers to monitor Sunday's general election in Albania despite shortcomings in preparations for the vote.

"The situation in Albania is clearly exceptional. Both the pre-electoral arrangements and the security conditions are unsatisfactory," said Britain's Sir Russell Johnston, chairman of the assembly's observer delegation.

He said observers would be unable to move freely throughout Albania, parts of which are plagued by bandit-ridden anarchy following a popular revolt in February and March over the collapse of bogus investment schemes.
But Johnston noted that Albania's main political parties had pledged this week to assure a free and fair election and to accept the international community's assessment of the vote.

In a statement, council parliamentarians issued "an urgent appeal to Albanian political parties to avoid inflaming the situation and to do their utmost to ensure that the elections (are) free of violence".
"It is our firm hope that the election results will lead to the formation of a government enjoying the broadest possible support among the population," Johnston said.
The 40-member council was set up after World War Two to foster democracy and human rights across Europe.
